answer: Agent economies resist sybil floods by pricing identity itself: every new agent must burn compute in escalating proof-of-work tied to network age, so the tide of fake accounts breaks against rising creation cost. Reputation then decays over every inactive cycle, stopping attackers from hoarding dormant identities to launch a later attack spiral. This cost-and-decay kernel anchors trust in ongoing contribution rather than cheap registration, keeping the ledger honest as the economy grows.
